newsitem.title: UK: Calais fishermen lift blockade of port.
newsitem.headline: Calais fishermen lift blockade of port.

text.p: Fishermen blockading the port of Calais have ceased their action this morning pending the outcome of talks being held in Paris, a spokesman for the port told Reuters this morning.
Port of Calais spokesman Gerard Baron said: "The fishermen have finished their action. We hope it is permanent and they do not restart the blockade after their meeting in Paris with the minister."
Baron added the fishermen ended their action at 1015 local time (0815 am) and allowed the freight ferry the "Nord-Pas de Calais" to enter port.
A spokesman for the Dover Harbour Board confirmed that the ferry had been allowed into Calais and that the blockade had also been lifted at the port of Boulogne, according to its information.

A Stena Line spokesman said it had also heard the action had ended and that the company would be sending the Stena Fantasia from Dover to Calais at 11.45 after it had arrived from Zeebrugge, where it had been diverted during the action.

P&O European Ferries earlier told Reuters its ferry the Pride of Burgundy had sailed for Calais in the hope that the blockade might be lifted by the time the Paris talks between the fishermen's' union and the Ministry of Agriculture ended. The vessel was due to arrive at Calais around 0945 GMT.

The P&O spokeswoman said the ship would have diverted to Zeebrugge if the blockade had stayed in place so as not to inflame the situation. She said the vessel was carrying 515 passengers and 87 trucks.

She added that P&O would be able to put a normal service back into operation within an hour of the blockade ending although there would be a backlog of traffic to be moved. --Paul Berrill, Reuters Shipping News + 44 171 542 4087
